evidence: BLOCK LEVEL, REPRODUCED. Qi et al. (2025, Sci Data 12:1755) publish Cronbach's alpha for this exact sample as .91 (positive affect) and .88 (negative affect). The shipped assignment -- PA_1..PA_9 = the 9 positive adjectives, NA_1..NA_9 = the 9 negative ones, stored raw with no reversal -- gives .906 and .876 over the 134 respondents, deviations of .0045 and .0043. Rivals: swapping one item across blocks gives .839/.800; all 18 as one unreversed scale gives .675; reverse-scoring any single item drops its block to .782 (PA) / .765 (NA). WITHIN-BLOCK ORDER, NOT ESTABLISHED. Predicting the NA correlation matrix from the instrument's semantic facets -- fear {NA_1 afraid, NA_3 nervous, NA_6 terrified, NA_9 jittery}, self-conscious {NA_2 guilty, NA_7 ashamed}, anger {NA_4 angry, NA_8 irritable}, sadness {NA_5 sad} -- and scoring mean(within-facet r) minus mean(between-facet r) over all 9! = 362,880 relabellings, the shipped order scores -0.0012 against a best of +0.1627 and a mean of +0.0000, ranking 175,681st of 362,880 (top 48.4%): chance. A second route also failed: per-item correlations with a correctly keyed Rosenberg total (Esteem 3,5,8,9,10 reversed, alpha .885 vs the paper's .89) run PA 0.21-0.57 and NA -0.24 to -0.53 with no content pattern, and 羞愧的/ashamed (NA_7), predicted to be the most esteem-negative NA item, is the least at -0.24. So the route pins the polarity block and the absence of reverse-coding and distinguishes NO item from the other eight in its own block -- PARTIAL, not VERIFIED. Re-runnable as verify_qi_2025_panas.R (VERDICT: PASS on the block-level claim; it prints the within-block negative result rather than omitting it).

What this does NOT establish: the order of the ten items WITHIN the reverse block, and it cannot separate SCC_6 from SCC_11 -- swapping either pair's item_text leaves every number above unchanged, and alpha is invariant to reversing the complement of a set. Route 3 (published reliability) + route 6 (keying polarity), on 134 respondents. The RSES has two widely circulated orderings of the same ten sentences and the paper prints no item list, so the shipped ordering is a testable claim. Cronbach's alpha published by Qi et al. (2025) for this exact sample = 0.89. Reverse-scoring the shipped (UMD-form) reverse set {Esteem_3,5,8,9,10} gives 0.8853; the rival ordering's reverse set {2,5,6,8,9} gives -2.7572; no reversal gives 0.0198. Correlation signs agree item by item: Esteem_1/2/4/6/7 average r = +0.616 / +0.608 / +0.605 / +0.662 / +0.641 within the positive block and -0.358 / -0.343 / -0.270 / -0.419 / -0.416 against the reverse block, and Esteem_3/5/9/10 the mirror (-0.571/-0.448/-0.520/-0.517 vs +0.467/+0.378/+0.509/+0.514). Esteem_8 is the known Chinese-RSES anomaly (item-rest +0.193, mean r -0.126 with the other reverse items) and is nonetheless in the authors' reverse set: excluding it from the reversal gives alpha 0.9085 against the published 0.89. Response direction confirmed separately from item means (positive-worded 3.09-3.30, reverse-worded 1.66-2.16 on 1-4), matching the paper's stated 1=strongly disagree..4=strongly agree and NOT the 1=STRONGLY AGREE numbering printed on the UMD form. What this does NOT establish: the order of items within a polarity class -- swapping the shipped text of Esteem_1 and Esteem_2, or of Esteem_9 and Esteem_10, would change none of the numbers above. Hence PARTIAL. Re-runnable: verify_qi_2025_self_esteem.R, VERDICT: PASS.
